links.comparator_used: Zero-shot prompting with instructions only (also compared with annotated few-shot prompts)
links.outcome: Information extraction performance and hallucination rate
links.effect: Few-shot prompting significantly improved performance and reduced hallucinations; no numeric values given in the abstract
links.quote: Few-shot prompting and native-language inputs significantly improve performance and reduced hallucinations.

links.comparator_used: General-purpose small language models (e.g., LLaMA 3.1 8B) compared with biomedical models
links.outcome: Clinical information extraction performance from Italian EHRs, especially binary features
links.effect: General-purpose models outperformed biomedical models in most tasks, particularly binary features; no numeric values given in the abstract
links.tradeoff: Multiclass variables (TNM staging, PD-L1, ECOG-PS) remained harder because of implicit language and lack of standardization
links.quote: We show that general-purpose models (e.g., LLaMA 3.1 8B) outperform biomedical models in most tasks, particularly in extracting binary features.

design_hint: prompt design (few-shot, annotated examples, native-language prompts) with clinician input
